fiveClaims.old: Every finding includes a full visual and step-by-step AI Reasoning Trace. This allows safety managers to inspect the exact reasoning sequence, inputs used, and matched logic that led to the recommendations.
fiveClaims.whyExceeded: The string 'Reasoning Trace' appeared in the entire frontend exactly once — in that sentence. No such surface exists. The nearest real thing is Expert-only, Pro-only and capped at 1/day.
fiveClaims.replacement: Each finding records the facts HazLenz used and where each one came from — your observation text, your confirmation, or the inspection's regulatory context — the passage it flagged from, why a standard was or was not supported, and what the conclusion does not cover. The generated report carries the same basis, so a reviewer can evaluate the finding rather than take it on trust.
fiveClaims.evidence: Every element named is rendered today and was captured in the §318 corpus: per-fact provenance, the quoted span, the decision explanation, 'What limits this conclusion', 'What this assessment does not cover', and the report's Basis and Limitations block.

fiveClaims.old: Autonomously identifies missing or ambiguous parameters—such as worker proximity, equipment operational state, or control status—and flags them as critical questions to resolve before finalizing findings.
fiveClaims.whyExceeded: CLAIMS-GUARDRAILS.md prohibits 'autonomous'. This was its only live use, on the one feature whose purpose is to stop and ask a person.
fiveClaims.replacement: Identifies missing or ambiguous facts — worker proximity, equipment operational state, control status — and raises them as questions to settle before a finding is finalised. When a fact it depends on is unresolved, it says so and lowers its own confidence rather than assuming an answer.
fiveClaims.evidence: §318 measured the behaviour live: the unresolved fact was named, the settling question offered, and the standard stayed Candidate/Low until a person answered.

fiveClaims.old: To support repeatable validation and reasoning consistency, the engine's observation understanding is supported by an automated multi-scenario benchmark covering core industrial hazard scenarios.
fiveClaims.whyExceeded: §158 measured two executions of byte-identical verifier input, provider-attested at identical token counts, returning DIFFERENT verdicts. 'repeatable' and 'consistency' are prohibited.
fiveClaims.replacement: An automated multi-scenario benchmark exercises the deterministic engine's observation understanding during development. It is a development instrument, not a measured product accuracy rate, and we do not publish one. The Expert layer's answers are not guaranteed to be identical between runs on identical input.
fiveClaims.evidence: The benchmark exists and is still described. §158 for the instability; the formal evaluation failed and was not accepted, so no rate is published.

fiveClaims.old: Create a PIN to protect encrypted local inspection reports on this device.
fiveClaims.whyExceeded: AES-GCM is real, but getDeviceKey() writes 32 random bytes base64 in CLEARTEXT to localStorage beside the ciphertext, and pinSecurity.ts stores a salted SHA-256 of the PIN in the same store and never touches the key. The PIN does not gate decryption.
fiveClaims.replacement: Add a PIN lock for local inspection reports on this device. / This PIN is a lock screen for this device. Local reports are stored encrypted on the device, and the key is held on the device too — so the PIN keeps a passer-by out of the app, and it is not protection against someone who has the device itself. Your inspections on your Safety InSite account are not affected by this PIN.
fiveClaims.evidence: lib/encryption.ts and lib/pinSecurity.ts, traced at §318. The MECHANISM WAS NOT CHANGED.

fiveClaims.old: Matches structured observations against approved MSHA and OSHA (General Industry and Construction) regulatory frameworks to surface potentially applicable standard families and standards-informed references for qualified safety review.
fiveClaims.whyExceeded: Citation selection is code-resident and corpus-independent (KG-3F: 'citation SELECTION entirely in code with no database access'). 132 rule-declared citations have no governed record at all.
fiveClaims.replacement: Applies governed applicability rules to the observation to suggest potentially applicable MSHA and OSHA (General Industry and Construction) standards for qualified review. It shows how confident it is and whether the regulatory text for each citation has completed source review. It does not decide which standard legally applies.
fiveClaims.evidence: standard-applicability.rules.ts; KG-3F's rule-to-corpus map; the product's own confidenceLimitReason.
